newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips lower with crude in muted trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips lower with crude in muted trade.

text.p: Naphtha lost up to $2 a tonne on Friday, suffering under the weight of easier crude and muted demand.
Although swaps were slow and physical quieter, March was heard done at $214 twice, and $220 and $220.50 concluded for February.
A wet light virgin 4,500 tonne parcel was sold at cif high quotes +$3.75 cif Antwerp.
High freight rates continued to be a source of frustration making transatlantic business and cross Mediterranean deals had to formulate.
Some traders said the situation was unlikely to improve over the next week or so, but already there were glimmers of hope.
Shipbrokers said on Friday 27,500 tonne naphtha carriers going cross Med were seen commanding around W300 from W330 this time last week.
With the market showing clear backwardation there has been no incentive to pick up material and most end-users have been holding back if possible.
"Little bits and pieces have going all week and I expect the same next week," said one trader.
